title: Chronological kernel span reconstruction and NVTX envelope synthesis
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: kernel-level telemetry today is noisy for asynchronous, multi-stream execution. NVTX ranges are emitted by high-level runtime phases (prefill/decode) but async kernel launches, stream linking, and out-of-order GPU execution produce NVTX envelopes that no longer strictly contain the per-kernel execution windows. That leads to poor attribution of per-kernel metrics (time, SM utilization, memory) to logical spans, making cost/latency analysis and regression detection brittle.

Goal: build a deterministic, low-overhead pipeline that reconstructs chronological kernel spans and synthesizes a corrected NVTX envelope per request. The pipeline should stitch kernels into logical spans (prefill vs decode vs misc) even when kernels run out-of-order across streams, support sampling to control overhead, and provide a fallback mapping for kernels without clear stream-affinity.

Non-goal: this ticket does not implement UI surfacing; telemetry ingestion and storage format are in scope, small dashboarding smoke-tests are included but full Console integration will be follow-up.
acceptance_criteria: A mapping exists that assigns >=95% of observed kernel events to a logical span label (prefill/decode/other) for our standard performance corpus (1000 sampled requests across models: mix of short and long-seq).
End-to-end added overhead for a 1% continuous sampling rate is <1.5% wall-time on p3.16xlarge equivalent workloads (measured with microbench harness).
Telemetry ingestion schema includes: host_monotonic_ts_ns, gpu_launch_ts_ns, stream_id, kernel_fingerprint, inferred_span, original_nvtx_ranges, synthesized_nvtx_envelope.
CI tests cover slot-envelope merging, watermark-based ordering, and kernel-fingerprint collision edge cases.
A lightweight Grafana panel demonstrates before/after attribution for two benchmark prompts and is linked in the ticket.
Feature gated behind runtime flag runtime.observability.envelope_rewrite with rollout plan to 10%/50%/100%.
Documentation: Confluence design doc and telemetry schema uploaded and linked.
work_items: Design: define slotted-envelope algorithm and watermarking heuristics (host + GPU timestamps).
Instrument runtime to emit per-kernel minimal fingerprint and host monotonic stamp at launch. Avoid blocking hot path (use buffered writer).
Ingest pipeline: implement envelope synthesizer that orders kernels by (gpu_ts || host_ts) per request and emits inferred_span for each kernel event.
Sampling: implement probabilistic sampling and burst-safe sampling to capture tail requests with low overhead.
Fallback heuristics: fingerprint-based similarity, stream-affinity fallback, and time-window coalescing for ambiguous kernels.
Validation: build microbench harness with controlled out-of-order kernels, produce golden mapping, and assert accuracy thresholds.
Create dashboards and alerts for mapping-failures ratio and sampling overhead regressions.
Rollout: implement feature flag, smoke tests, and gradual ramp plan with on-call playbook.
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial design meeting with runtime and observability. Decided on slotted-envelope approach rather than strictly binding NVTX to streams to tolerate racing kernels.

2026-02-18: Prototype emitter added to prefill path. Emits kernel fingerprint (sha1 of kernel name + params) and host_monotonic_ts at launch. Microbench shows per-request overhead ~0.6% at 1% sample rate.

2026-02-25: Ingest-side synthesizer PoC implemented in telemetry-service branch (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry-service/pull/498). Uses host_ts as tiebreaker when GPU timestamps are missing.
2026-03-03: Ran corpus of 2k requests across gpt-like long-seq model. Mapping accuracy 91% with default heuristics; debug showed ambiguity for short 1-2ms kernels launched on helper streams.

2026-03-06: Added stream-affinity scoring and kernel-fingerprint clustering; mapping accuracy improved to 96% on the same corpus. Noted 0.1% collision rate for fingerprint; added collision detection and fallback to strong-fingerprint (sha256) for flagged cases.
2026-03-10: Integration test added to CI job perf-telemetry-suite. Dashboard mock-up available at https://grafana.internal/redwood/runtime/envelope-rewrite.
2026-03-12: Addressed reviewer feedback on memory overhead and replaced in-memory event buffer with ring buffer to cap resident memory per worker. Preparing PR
reviewer_feedback: Rajiv Patel (observability): please quantify worst-case memory use for bursty scenarios and add backpressure behaviour — suggested ring buffer + drop-on-overflow with telemetry counters.
Li Wei (runtime): avoid introducing host-side blocking writes on hot path; suggested using per-thread batching with a single atomic enqueue and background flush.
Nina O'Connor (security): confirm that kernel fingerprints do not include customer data. Marked security_review_required true — schedule a short review with Security.
Product (Elena Markov): prefer default rollout flag off; require 10% production night-run before enabling for standard accounts.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: stronger heuristics reduce misattribution but increase computation on ingest. We bias toward ingest compute (cluster-side) to avoid hot-path runtime overhead.
Sampling strategy: default 1% continuous + 0.5% burst capture for requests that trigger fallback heuristics. This balances statistical coverage for regressions and production cost.
Future: expose synthesized envelope and inferred_span in Console UI with token-level attribution for regressions and quality alerts (separate ticket).
